summary: The note argues that fair trade ingredients are central to ethical regional cuisine, linking local food traditions to fair wages, environmental standards and sustainability. It cites chefs and a cooperative farmer, reinterprets classic dishes with fair trade ingredients, and gives a recipe for Fair Trade Chocolate Alfajores. It closes by stressing consumer education and everyday purchasing choices as drivers of a more equitable food system.
one_line: Fair trade ingredients can make regional cuisine more ethical, illustrated by chef examples, farmer testimony and a fair trade chocolate alfajores recipe.
key_facts: As of September 21, 2023, fair trade certification has broadened beyond coffee, chocolate and bananas to many products integral to regional cuisines worldwide.
The fair trade label guarantees ingredients were cultivated under strict standards of ethical employment, environmental practices and equitable trade conditions.
Maria Gonzalez owns the farm-to-table restaurant "Terra Madre" in San Francisco and spoke at the Sustainable Food Conference in Portland on October 5, 2023.
Fair trade vanilla pods from Madagascar come from small-scale farms where farmers are guaranteed a minimum price for their harvest.
In November 2023, the author spoke with Thomas Bekele, a member of a fair trade cooperative in Ethiopia that produces heirloom varietal spices.
Thomas Bekele said: "Before fair trade, it was difficult to predict my earnings year over year," and that he can now invest in better farming practices.
On September 14, 2023, at the Food Ethics Summit in Rome, Italian chef Luca Monti demonstrated fair trade olive oil from cooperatives in Palestine in his dish "Fettuccine al Raggio di Sole".
Argentinian alfajores are sandwich cookies filled with dulce de leche and coated in chocolate; the recipe uses fair trade sugar, dulce de leche and dark chocolate.
The alfajores recipe uses 2 cups flour, 3/4 cup fair trade sugar, 2 eggs, 1 cup fair trade dulce de leche, 8 ounces fair trade dark chocolate and 1 tbsp coconut oil.
The dough is chilled for 30 minutes, rolled about 1/4 inch thick, and baked at 350°F (175°C) for 10-12 minutes.
After baking, cookies are sandwiched with dulce de leche and dipped halfway into melted dark chocolate mixed with coconut oil.
In 2023, Fair Trade USA and the World Fair Trade Organization ran educational campaigns to raise consumer awareness of fair trade.
The note concludes that every fair trade purchase and meal acts as a vote for a more equitable and sustainable future.
